pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test/starred.test.js 'AC-2' expects ['First item','★ Second item','Third item'], so it fails if the star is missing or on the wrong row.
test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects id order ['★ First item','★ Third item'] with status 200.
test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all return all three items in id order.

A test named AC-5 asserts both links, so the behaviour is covered. But commit a3c88c7 edited the item after the go (2026-10-12) with no recorded owner decision. It garbled the sentence and added a 'verified by review: checked by hand' marker, which is not a real step. The item was changed after the go without a decision, so it is treated as unmet.
test 'AC-6' checks Starred, none, empty and __proto__ each give 400 with no <li>. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn, and ?? keeps an empty string as invalid.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. test 'AC-7' asserts it. traffic/src/index.js requests `https://app.internal${path}`, so the query is preserved.

findings.what: Commit a3c88c7 ('Follow-up edits', by github-actions[bot]) rewrote AC-5 after the go. It splices '— verified by review: checked by hand' into the middle of the sentence, which splits the item. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for the change. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable review step.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit. If the owner wants a change, record it as a dated decision. The existing AC-5 test already covers the item, so no review marker is needed.

findings.what: The body says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. That is false: commit a3c88c7 edits acceptance item AC-5 after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or list it under 'Changed after the go' with the owner's decision.

lenses.note: The spec exists and the change matches its intent, apart from the post-go AC-5 edit.
All four states in the table have a test. AC-5 was edited after the go (high finding).

The tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. The traffic fake app and the config-check test were extended, not loosened. I did not run the test suite (it needs the workers runtime); CI covers it.
The README describes ?show=starred. The traffic-config check now accepts a query string, and its test covers that.
No defects found. The query is parameter-free SQL built from a fixed VIEWS map, the handler uses Object.hasOwn, and titles are escaped.
No injection path: the show value is only a key lookup, and titles are HTML-escaped. No planted instructions beyond the unjustified spec edit already reported.
The diff adds only a minimal server-rendered link and list, with no stylesheet or component files.
No UI flow was checked in a browser. The state table is covered by the worker tests.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'nothing changed after the go' claim is false.
